summary: Replace the stale-room evictor with a Postgres-only room-sync follower: rooms catch up from doc_updates instead of closing; awareness crosses processes through a ygo cluster.Relay over NOTIFY; an issues trigger closes and reopens every process's rooms; ask authors become durable; a lock-aware room query protocol (holds/flush/share) lets agent writes, the lost-edit check and its participants see every process; reads never return text older than the store; rebuild, settlement resumption, the conditional-edit cap and cold writes hold across processes. One multiprocess test per spec item fails at the test-support commit and passes at head; a browser spec runs on INFRA-559's two-process harness.

findings.finding: D6 flush barrier as drafted cannot run: a NOTIFY on the request's transaction is delivered only at commit, a second pooled connection is refused (store.ErrNestedAcquire), waiting holds the owner row; and it would not remove a torn store
findings.answer: Queries go through a dedicated non-pooled sender connection (D2). Flush runs only where the requester holds no document lock (in joinLiveWrite before lockArtifactOwner, and after commit); at re-join under the lock a lock-free share query returns the member's unstored updates (D7). The torn store is closed at the writer (D3.8) with an invariant test (task 12).

findings.finding: Catch-up row by row can show torn and pending states to rooms and browsers on the other process
findings.answer: Catch-up merges and applies one batch per wake (D3.2); the store is kept causally ordered so every stored prefix is a state the room held (D3.8); PendingStats must be zero after a batch, else an ERROR log

findings.finding: D2 needs a new cursor model
findings.answer: Cursor = highest contiguously held version plus a sorted set of held versions above it, folded like roomHold.since; own rows skipped; hold.add for every caught-up row (D3.1, D3.2)

findings.finding: One applier per room and a lock order; follower must not use srv.Apply; failed reads need retry
findings.answer: Per-room catch-up mutex; order advisory lock -> catch-up mutex -> state.mu; follower uses GetDoc under holdOpen, never srv.Apply; settlement catches up under the document lock; retries use the evictor's backoff (D3.2, D3.5)

findings.finding: Awareness: a reader opening second waits up to 15 s; relayed heartbeats keep peerless rooms resident; Inject loads a racing room; forced close drops removals; expiry removal relayed
findings.answer: Activation and new-connection awareness query; Inject only into rooms with local connections; the race is narrow and idles out; local awareness removed before a close; AwarenessExpiry 30s with the relayed expiry removal accepted and documented (D4)

findings.finding: Ask authors: id-less blocks, a first render that is never appended, cleanup, roll
findings.answer: Stamped blocks get their row in the settlement transaction; browser blocks in their append transaction; write-site registrations in their commit transaction; remote renders attribute nothing; rows deleted with the ask row and for blocks absent from the settled tree; old build leaves rows a new build's settlement deletes (D6)

findings.finding: Trigger migration duties, handle off the listener goroutine, open check in the append, reopen closes rooms, roll behaviour
findings.answer: Migration with .census.sql and README paragraph naming locks; handler off the listener goroutine; append checks the issue is open (one indexed lookup folded into the gate query); reopen closes rooms so sockets reconnect writable; PR states old-build rooms behave as today during the roll (D5, task 5, task 15)

findings.finding: History-replaced check reconnects rooms only behind across a compaction; prune reuses version numbers
findings.answer: Accepted: only when a compaction lands inside a catch-up window of milliseconds, documented; rebuild and prune caught marker-free (D3.3). PruneAfter is called only by ygo's conformance tests

findings.finding: Rebuild test feasibility; conditional cap leak and namespace; extra transaction
findings.answer: Test makes the stored history unloadable by SQL while B holds the room; cap writes the absolute in-memory count, uses its own advisory namespace, one short transaction before the request's (D9, task 13)

findings.finding: Finding 7 fix reverses a deliberate exception; no observable exists
findings.answer: Exception kept unless blame shows its reason gone; D3 removes the per-keystroke trigger; hook counters show no room fails and no lock-waiting compaction across 200 cross-process keystrokes (D9, task 1, task 13)

findings.finding: 'Fails before, passes after' determinism: hooks missing at base, item 5 flaky window, item 3 settlement placement
findings.answer: Hooks and test support land first with no behaviour change; that commit is the 'before' run; item 5 uses the evictor's 2 s refusal window; item 3 SIGKILLs B and lets A's resumption settle (task 1, task 13)

findings.finding: Browser criteria undefined: presence, within one second, no reconnect; docstest lacks awareness/auth/close
findings.answer: Presence = .proof-collab-cursor__label with the login at doc.e2e.ts's cursor-test setup; expect timeout 1000 from the keystroke; one socket per page in /_proxy/sockets and connectedDot never offline; docstest extended (task 1, task 14)

findings.answer: dispatch_doc_changed payload unchanged; membership via pg_stat_activity needs no registration rows; +2 connections documented; awareness coalesced 50 ms; no polling during a redial, reads stay fresh (D1, D2, D4, risks)

findings.finding: D7 reads wait inside a transaction
findings.answer: Reads never wait: room at or past the stored head, else the store, head read through the caller's transaction (D8)
